html:
SMTO-TSK-0036 — Your update to the running task is empty or too long

GUID: 86f88216-a572-4f95-a36e-599d69689465
Slug: steering-input-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The update you sent to the running task was blank or longer than 24,000 characters, so SMTO didn't send it. Your text stays in the box.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the box under the running task that says "Steer this run…". Make sure it contains actual words, not just spaces or blank lines. SMTO won't pass an empty update to a task.
  2. If your update is very long, shorten it to under 24,000 characters, or split it into separate updates. Updates over 24,000 characters are too large to add to a running task.
  3. Select Steer (or Retry steer) again. Once the text fits, SMTO can pass it to the task.

What success looks like

  • Your update appears in the conversation and the task carries on with it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the same oversized text again; shorten it first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Steering input for a running task was not a string, contained only whitespace, or exceeded 24,000 characters.

What this means

  • Steering input is not a string, contains only whitespace or exceeds 24000 characters. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Steering input is not a string, contains only whitespace or exceeds 24000 characters.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect amendment type, non-whitespace content and character count without altering accepted earlier steering.

How to fix it

  • Send a non-blank steering string of 1–24,000 characters through the run's steer control (RunStore.steer). Previously accepted amendments are unaffected.
  • Supply 1 to 24000 characters of intended user steering through the active task’s supported steering control.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A bounded nonempty amendment is accepted once under its intended submission identity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
